messages:
alex: Heads up — noticed python sdk (v0.8.2) drops rate-limit headers on 429 responses when using AsyncClient. Can't read Retry-After or X-RateLimit-Remaining. Pretty bad for client-side throttling. Repro below.

alex: repro: ```py
from redwood import RedwoodClient
async def f():
    c = RedwoodClient(api_key="REDACTED")
    # hit our throttling quickly with small model + tight loop
    for _ in range(50):
        try:
            await c.chat.create(model="small-test", input="hi")
        except Exception as e:
            # expecting headers like Retry-After, X-RateLimit-Remaining
            print(type(e).__name__, e.response.headers)
```

maria: I can repro on sync client too occasionally — seems headers available on 200 but missing on 429. Might be httpx behaviour when response body is consumed/stream closed.

sam: logging shows httpx response.raw.headers contain them, but our wrapper Response.headers filters unknown keys (we canonicalize header names). Investigating whether our error path loses them.

jordan: FWIW we standardize on: Retry-After, X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset. SDK should expose a RateLimitInfo object + Response.rate_limit property. Also a small client-side Throttler utility would help folks implementing backoff rather than reinventing.

alex: +1. Ideally include parsed fields: reset as int unix seconds, remaining as int, limit as int, retry_after as float (seconds). Typing + docs please.

maria: Proposal: add `get_rate_limit(response) -> Optional[RateLimitInfo]` on client utils and `TooManyRequestsError.rate_limit: Optional[RateLimitInfo]`. For async flows, also provide `AsyncThrottler` with `async with throttler.acquire()` semantics that sleeps until reset when needed.

sam: I'll open an issue + rough PR with tests that assert headers survive error wrapping. Will also add a tiny helper that reads both Retry-After and X-RateLimit-Reset for fallback.

deploy-bot: PR #789 opened by sam: feature/sdk-rateheaders — tests added. CI started. :rocket:

jordan: Can we use a typed dataclass in the public surface: `class RateLimitInfo(TypedDict): limit: int; remaining: int; reset: int; retry_after: float` so static typing works nicely for users?

alex: That would be great for my team's typed code. Also please add example snippet to docs showing how to wire client-side throttling with `AsyncThrottler`.

sam: Created issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/123 and draft RFC at https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/789. Labels: devex, sdk, async, rate-limit. Assigning to @jordan for API design review. Will follow up with a small sample app in examples/ that uses AsyncThrottler.

jordan: Acked. I'll review API shapes tomorrow. If we agree, plan: (1) make headers passthrough on error, (2) add RateLimitInfo typed object, (3) implement AsyncThrottler util and add to docs/examples.

alex: Thanks — this will reduce a lot of copy/paste logic in our infra. :+1:

sam: I'll update the PR with tests and a sample snippet in examples/rate_limit_throttler.py. Closing for now, will ping when PR is ready for review.
